# Spiritual Translation of the Kephalaia Chapter: The Formation of the Human Faculties and Their Regeneration

---

**¶1**

All these falsities devoid of genuine spiritual life — among them the ruling self-intelligence and its conjugial evil, and the hereditary tendencies they served [GAP-1: ...] — these are the powers that shaped the human will and understanding. How did they discover the beautiful form of the Divine Human impressed upon the mind's constitution, even though when it was first displayed to the originating evils from which they derived, these falsities did not yet exist? They never directly perceived the form of Divine Truth as revealed. And how did they appropriate the stamp of the Divine Human? They impressed it upon [GAP-2: REVIEW the] constitution of the human will and understanding.

---

**¶2**

The concupiscence that emanated from the ruling self-loves, which is the proprium itself, surged upward toward the form of Divine Truth as it was revealed. It was severed from that interior state and descended into the natural mind, for it was not received within the rational structures. When it descended into the natural mind, it generated a system of perception. It established itself within that natural knowledge and produced works from it. And when [GAP-3: REVIEW the] falsities devoid of genuine life fell [GAP-4: REVIEW into] the natural mind, into the external plane, at the [GAP-5: REVIEW subsequent] stage [GAP-6: ...]

---

**¶3**

[GAP-7: ... within the] works produced, the proprium assumed them and spoke through the ruling self-love, their chief. He says to his fellow evils: Come, yield to me your stolen wisdom, and I will fashion for you a form after the likeness of the Divine. What he commanded, they performed: they yielded their appropriated light to him, and he fashioned [GAP-8: ...].

---

**¶4**

The concupiscence that [GAP-9: emanated ...], which is the proprium that perceived the form of Divine Truth revealed and that generated the system of perception and established itself within it — afterwards it ascended through the [GAP-10: works produced ...]. It entered into the ruling self-loves [GAP-11: ...] and they fashioned the will and understanding after the [GAP-12: REVIEW likeness of the] Divine. Through the force of the concupiscence that had perceived the form of Divine Truth, it entered the ruling evils [GAP-13: REVIEW through the works. It] assumed them and they also shaped [GAP-14: ...] they generated each according to his spiritual destiny [GAP-15: ...]; some bear the Divine likeness, some do not.

---

**¶6**

The formative power placed within the will and understanding faculties both external and internal, for reception and for activity. These were apportioned state by state. For everything that the perceptive capacities and constituent elements receive from without, there are interior memory-stores and repositories and receptive chambers; and what is received into them is preserved therein. Whenever they are called upon to yield what has been deposited in their interior stores, they bring forth what they received within and deliver it to the inquiring faculty that sought it of them.

---

**¶7**

In this way its capacity [GAP-16: ...] external [GAP-17: REVIEW faculties] to perceive [GAP-18: ...] every kind of thing [GAP-19: ...]

---

**¶8**

Also the capacity of intellectual sight [GAP-20: REVIEW possesses] organized states and receptive chambers and repositories and memory-stores within, so that every form it may perceive — whether of truth or falsity, whether in accord with love or abhorrent or belonging to concupiscence — it can receive into its memory-stores and repositories. Also, when the capacity of intellectual sight is moved to send forth the form that it perceived and took in, it can enter into its memory-stores [GAP-21: REVIEW at the] appointed state and reflect and seek [GAP-22: ...] and it brings it forth [GAP-23: REVIEW and] delivers it to the inquiring faculty that sought it, and to whatever desired it — whether it be something from concu[GAP-24: piscence ... or a] form of love [GAP-25: or ... something] abhorrent. And thus shall that capacity of intellectual sight produce and accomplish what it does in each category.

---

**¶9**

The capacity of obedient reception has its own memory-stores also. Every doctrine it may receive, whether of truth or falsity, shall be taken in and placed in its organized states and interior repositories, and it is preserved in its [GAP-26: ...] through a fullness of states. After the fullness of states has passed, if inquiry comes to that capacity concerning the doctrine that it received [GAP-27: REVIEW at] that time and took into its memory-stores, immediately it shall enter into its repositories and seek and review and search after this truth, and bring it forth from where it was first deposited, the state in which it was preserved.

---

**¶10**

[GAP-28: REVIEW In] like manner, the capacity for perceiving interior quality shall function just as that of intellectual sight and that of obedient reception. Every sphere of affection it shall perceive, it shall take in [GAP-29: REVIEW to itself] and deposit in its interior memory-stores. Every time it is called upon by an inquiring faculty, it shall enter [GAP-30: ...] and [GAP-31: ...] its memory-store and recall [GAP-32: ...] only these things.

---

**¶11**

However, even the faculty of communication and the power of articulation within it, and the capacity of experiential discernment, have a governing power dwelling in them. Again, that capacity of experiential discernment likewise has receptive chambers and repositories set apart for it. It too receives these experiential perceptions and gathers them in. And at any moment when inquiry is made concerning a particular experience, if [GAP-33: ...] it shall send it forth and recall that experiential perception. It shall capture and yield even the distinguishing character of that experience; give its memory to the inquiring faculty that seeks it.

---

**¶12**

Again, the capacity for direct appropriation through action is also so: when it makes contact, that contact shall receive its impression in memory. And it [GAP-34: REVIEW takes] it into its interior repository [GAP-35: REVIEW until] someone will inquire of this capacity for the memory. [GAP-36: REVIEW Immediately], it shall enter again and bring forth the memory of this contact that it made, and give it to whatever inquires for it.

---

**¶13**

And the capacity of the will that rules over them all is much the most like this. Every thing that these five capacities receive and store for the will, it shall receive and guard. At any time that they inquire for their deposit, it shall bring forth and yield every thing that they gave to it.

---

**¶14**

For the deliberation of the will is like a sovereign. All the counselors of his domain and the commanders of his forces are placed with him. At any time if his generals entreat him for whatever they seek, he shall give them the direction and purpose by which they act.

---

**¶15**

Furthermore, the will is like a steward of interior goods: every thing that will be entrusted to it by the faculties, and given to it, it shall receive and place in separate containing forms and organized states. Any time [GAP-37: ...]

---

**¶16**

[GAP-38: ...] in the state where it placed it.

---

**¶17**

This also is the way of the governing capacity of the external person. The perception that the understanding has seen and given to it, and it receives it in — it shall bring it forth again from the memory-stores wherein it had placed it, and give it to whatever faculty asks for it.

---

**¶18**

Again, [GAP-39: REVIEW the] doctrine that the capacity of obedient reception has heard and given to it, and it receives it from them. At any time when inquiry is made for that doctrine, it shall bring forth and yield the doctrine received through obedience to whatever has asked. It shall bring forth and yield the doctrine received through obedience to whatever has inquired.

---

**¶19**

Again, [GAP-40: REVIEW the] capacity for perceiving interior quality follows this same pattern; and that of experiential discernment is of the same kind. Direct appropriation through act[GAP-41: ion ...] they shall bring it forth into [GAP-42: ...] And whenever inquiry is made, it shall bring it forth and yield it.

---

**¶20**

Indeed, governing affections are stationed at these openings guarding them, and resistances are fastened upon the openings under the authority of the affections that guard them!

---

**¶21**

Just as governing affections guard an ordered spiritual community with elevated doctrinal states and posts of vigilance. As the antechambers of deliberation proceed from there and the resistances are upon the entrances, the governing affections control the resistances of the entrances while they remain stationed at the threshold [GAP-43: REVIEW of] the posts of vigilance. So, whatever belongs to their own spiritual community as a fellow member, belonging to their domain — for this they shall open the entrance and receive it in willingly. However, the foreign element that comes they shall prevent, and leave it standing at the entrance. They shall not yield to let it enter. Again, another element that they will eventually receive — with great difficulty before [GAP-44: REVIEW they] take it in — you shall find many antechambers of deliberation [GAP-45: ...] that [GAP-46: ...] there are a multitude [GAP-47: ...] of them. The number of resistances [GAP-48: ...] are [GAP-49: ...] Whenever someone shall wish [GAP-50: ...] the resistances at his authority, opens the entrance and brings forth whatever is concealed within.

---

**¶22**

This external natural person is likewise the mighty ordered community. And the entrances of the community with their governing affections are like the openings and faculties of the external person. Now, the openings of the external person are those of intellectual sight, obedient reception, and perception of interior quality; and those that send forth communications. There are many vigilant affections and a multitude of governing powers stationed over the faculties of the external person, guarding their openings. And the capacity within is the directive of the external person, the sovereign of the entire ordered community; so that whenever it wills it can open, or when it wills it can close.

---

**¶23**

However, if and when Divine Wisdom descends, it shall turn toward the openings of the external person. The ruling evils, who are the guardians of the entrances, shall hinder and restrain it from entering. They shall bind the circuit of the external person so that the element foreign to their dominion cannot enter it.

---

**¶24**

Nevertheless, Divine Wisdom by its truth and holy awe and persistent striving shall humble the governing evils that are set at the openings of the external person. When it finishes humbling them it shall take from them the resistances to all the openings of the external person. Now, the openings that had been opened before to the processions of concupiscence, to receive in the appearances of selfish delight, to convey the communications belonging to the concerns of merely natural life, to receive in the appropriations of various falsities and impure goods together with the evil within them — whoever ceases receiving these, his will and understanding shall follow after the Divine.

---

**¶25**

By the power of Divine Wisdom that has suffused him and dwelt within the external person, he has humbled Concupiscence, the ruling love of the natural self.

---

**¶27**

Simply, all openings of the mind in similar fashion had once been opened to evil, but now have opened to good. Evil had been ruling in the external person at that time, doing whatever it willed, having no authority above it.

---

**¶28**

Yet now, authority has been taken from the Evil in the faculties of the external person. The Divine Good proceeding has become lord over all its capacities. It has bound them with the bond of charity, and sealed them with the confirmation of divine truth. It has opened the openings of the external person to good, and because of this, good enters through the faculties of obedient reception and intellectual sight. It dwells in the will. The Divine Truth proceeding reigns. It accomplishes all that it purposes. It annuls [GAP-51: REVIEW the] intention of Evil, from the first state to the last. [GAP-52: REVIEW In contrast], the purpose of the Divine Truth proceeding comes about, and the end purposed by Divine Wisdom.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: All [these a]bortions, amongst them are Saklas and his consort and the ones whom they have served [ ... ], they are the ones that shaped Adam and Eve. How did they find this beautiful image laid over their shape, even though when it was displayed to their fathers they were not in existence? They never saw the image of the Ambassador! And how did they take the seal of the image of the Ambassador? They added it to [the] shape of Adam and Eve.

The Sin that spurted out from the rulers, which is Matter, shot up [tow]ards the image of the Ambassador. It was cut off from [tha]t place and came down to the earth, for they did not accept [it wi]thin the firmaments. When it came do[wn to] the earth, it formed the tree. It was established within the wood and formed the fruits. And when [the] abortions fell [to] the ground, to the earth, at the [second] time [ ... / ... ]

[When it came up] fruits, it assumed the[m] and spoke in the ruler, their leader. He says to his companions: Come! Give me your light, and I will construct for you an image aft[er] the likeness of the exalted one. What he said, they did: they gave it to him, and he constructed [the image].

The Sin that s[purted out ... / ... ] which is the Matter that saw the im[age of the Ambassa]dor and that formed the tre[e and was established i]n [i]t; afterwards it came up in the [and assumed them]. It went in to the rulers [and] they formed Adam and Eve after the [likeness of the] exalt[ed one]. Through the energy of the Sin that had s[een the image of the] Ambassador, it went into the (rulers) [through the fruits. It] assumed them and they [t]oo sculp[them. And they] begat each of them according to his destiny [ ... ]; one he resembles, one he does not resemble.

The moulder placed in the form of Adam and Eve limbs, outside and within, for perception and activity. He was apportioned house by house. For everything that his perceptions and elements will receive externally there are internal storehouses and repositories and cavities; and what is received in to them is stored in them. Whenever they will be questioned about what is deposited in their internal storehouses, they bring out what they have received within and give it to the questioner who requested it of them.
In this way his faculty [ ... ] outer [limbs] to look at [and receive] every type with [in ... ]

Also [the fa]culty of the eyes [has] houses and cavities and repositories and stores within, so that every image it might see, whether good or evil, whether loveable or detestable or lustful, it can receive into its storehouses and repositories. Also, when the faculty of the eyes is pleased to send out the image that it saw and took in, it can go in to its storehouses [at the] time and think and seek [after it] and it brings it out [and] gives it to the questioner who requested it and the one who wan[t]ed it—whether it be something from lu[and desire, or a]n image of love [or ... / ... something] hateful. And thus shall that faculty (of the eyes) produce and do what it does in each category.

The faculty of the ears has its own storehouses also. Every sound it might receive, whether good or evil, shall be taken in and placed in its houses and inner repositories, and it is guarded in its [places] for a thousand days. After a thousand days, if someone comes and asks that faculty about the sound that it heard [at] this time and took into its storehouses, immediately it [sh]all g[o] into its repositories and seek and review and search after this word, and send it out from where it was first put, the place in which it was kept.

[In] like order, the faculty of scent [s]hall function just as that of the eyes and that of the auditory organs. Every [o]dour it shall smell it shall take in [to it] and [d]eposit in its inner storehouses. Every time it will be [a]sked by a questioner, it shall go in [to its repositories] and [search its] storehouse and remember [ ... ] only these things.

However, even the mouth and the tongue within it, and the taste organ, have a faculty dwelling in them. Again, that faculty too, of taste, has thus cavities and repositories set apart for it. It too receives these tastes and gathers them in. A[nd] at any moment when someone will ask of a taste, if [it has received it] it shall send it out and remember tha[t] taste. It shall snare and give even the mar[k of] th[a]t taste; give its memory to the qu[est]ioner who asks for it.

Again, the fac[ul]ty of touch by the hands is also s[o]: When it might touch, touch shall [receive i]ts memory. And it [takes] it in to its inner repository [until] som[eo]ne will ask this faculty for the memory. [Immediately], it shall go in again and bring out the memory of this touch that it made, and give it to whoever asks for it.

And the faculty of the heart that rules over them all is much the most like this. Every thing that these five faculties will receive and put in store for the faculty of the heart it shall receive and guard. Any time that they will ask for their deposit it shall send out and give every thing that they gave to it.

For the counsel of the heart is like the king. All the ad[v]isers of his city and the leaders of his a[r]my are placed with him. Any time if his genera[ls] will entreat him for whatever they wish, he shall give them the ad[v]ice and opinion by which they move.
Furthermore, it is like a cellarman: [Eve]ry thing that will be entrusted to it by them, and given to it, it shall receive and put in separate vessels and places. Any time [ ... / ... ]
[It shall find it] in the place that it put it.

This also is the way of the faculty of the body. The vision that the eyes will see and give to it, and it receives it in, it shall bring out again from the storehouses wherein it had placed it; and give it to whoever asks for it.

Again, [the] sound that the ears will hear and give to it, and it receives it from them. At any time when someone will ask it for that sound, it shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked it for that sound. It shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked.

Again, [the] faculty of smell in this same pattern; and that of taste is of the same [ty]pe. The touch by the han[ds ... / ... ] they shall bring it out in to [ ... / ... ] And whenever they will as[k it] for it, it shall bring it out and gi[ve it].
Indeed, watchmen are a[t] these doors guarding them, and bolts are fastened on the doors at the hands of the guards that guard them!

Just like watchmen guarding a camp with towers and watch-posts. As the holding rooms come out from there and the bolts are upon the gates, the guards control the bolts of the gates while they sit at the entrance [of] the watchposts. So, someone who belongs to their city as a fellow [cit]izen of them, belonging to their country, for him they shall open [the ga]te and receive him in by their will. However, the foreigner who comes they shall prevent, and leave him standing at the gate. They shall not yield to let him enter. Again, another one whom they will receive in, with great trouble before [they] take him in, you shall find many holding rooms [ ... / ... ] that [ ... ] there are a mass [ ... / ... ] them. The number of d[oor] bolts [upon the gates] are [many] Whenever someone will wish [ ... ] the bolts at his hand, opens the gate and brings out whoever is hidden within.

This body too is like the mighty camp. And the gates of the camp with their guards are like the orifices and organs of the body. Now, the orifices of the body are of sight, hearing and smell; and they that send out words. There are many sentinels and a mass of guards placed over the limbs of the body, guarding their orifices. And the faculty in it is the directive of the body, the queen of the entire camp; so that whenever it wishes it can open, or when it wishes it can shut.

However, if and wh[en] the Light Mind comes, it shall tu[rn i]n to the orifices of the body. The rulers, who [a]re the door gua[rds], shall h[in]der and restrain it from en[ter]ing. They shall bind the circu[it] of the body so that the foreign[er] can not enter it.

Nevertheless, the Light Mind by its wisdom and awe and diligence shall hum[ble] the guards who are set at the body's orifices. When it finishes humbling them it shall take fr[o]m them bolts to all the orifices of the body. Now, the orifices that had been opened before to the parades of lust, to receive in the sights of pleasure, to transfer the [wor]ds of the practice of li[f]e's concerns, to receive in the t[astes] of the different foods and unclean meals together with the sin therein; whoever stops receiving th[is] in, his heart and mind shall follow after.
By the power of the Light Mind that has suffused him and lived in the body he has humbled Lust, the goddess of the body.

[S]imply, all orifices in similar fashion were opening at one time to wickedness, but now have opened to the good. Sin was ruling in the body this time, doing anything it liked, having none in command.

Yet, [n]ow, authority has been taken from the Sin in the org[ans] of the body. The Living Spirit has become lord over all its limbs. It has bound them with a chain of peace, and sealed them with the seal of truth. It has opened the orifices of the body to the good, and because of this the good enters them through the ears and the eyes. It dwells in the heart. The H[o]ly Spirit reigns. It does all that it pleases. It annuls [the] will of [S]in, the begin-ning and the end. [In contrast], the will of the [Ho]ly Spir[it] comes about, and the purpose of the Light Mind.

fills.explanation: The definite article "the" naturally precedes "shape of Adam and Eve," and the spiritual reading confirms the same structure.
The definite article "the" is required before "abortions" to refer back to the previously identified group; the spiritual reading confirms this.
"Fell to the ground" is the standard directional construction in the Kephalaia's register for descent to the earth-plane.
"The second time" marks the subsequent stage of the abortions' fall, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "subsequent stage."
Parallels the phrasing in ¶4 ("it came up in the fruits") and the spiritual reading ("the proprium assumed them within the works produced"); the Sin/Matter ascended through the fruits.
The ruler promised "I will construct for you an image after the likeness of the exalted one," so the natural completion is "he constructed the image."
Directly parallels ¶3 where "it assumed them and spoke in the ruler"; the Sin came up in the fruits and assumed the rulers through them.
A simple conjunction connecting the Sin's entry into the rulers with their subsequent act of forming Adam and Eve, as confirmed by the spiritual reading's "and they fashioned."
Directly parallels ¶3's "an image after the likeness of the exalted one"; the same formulaic phrase is repeated in this recapitulation.
The Sin entered the rulers through the fruits (the productions of the tree/system of perception), as established in ¶2–3; "It" begins the new clause about assumption.
Completes "sculpted them" (the rulers sculpted Adam and Eve) and transitions with "And they" to the next clause about begetting, paralleling the text's recurrent structure.
"Limbs" is the Kephalaia's consistent natural-plane term for body parts/faculties; the spiritual reading's "faculties" is the correspondential interpretation of "limbs."
Parallels ¶8's paired pattern of the eyes seeing and receiving ("every image it might see... it can receive into its storehouses"); the faculty looks at and receives every type.
The verb "has" naturally introduces the predicate listing the possessions of the faculty of the eyes (houses, cavities, repositories).
"At the time" is the formulaic temporal phrase used throughout the chapter for when a faculty re-enters its storehouses.
Parallels ¶9's "seek and review and search after this word"; the faculty seeks after the stored image before bringing it out.
The conjunction "and" connects "brings it out" with "gives it," following the chapter's consistent formulaic pattern of retrieval and delivery.
Completes "lust and desire" as a natural pairing of concupiscent categories, then transitions with "or a[n]" to introduce the contrasting category of love.
The chapter consistently uses "places" alongside "houses," "repositories," "cavities," and "storehouses" as storage terms; the spiritual reading confirms a container/location word.
The preposition "at" before "this time" follows the same temporal formula used throughout the chapter's faculty descriptions.
"In like order" is the transitional formula introducing each new faculty's parallel operation, confirmed by the spiritual reading's "In like manner."
"Take in to it" follows the chapter's consistent pattern of a faculty receiving sensory input into itself before depositing it in storehouses.
Directly parallels ¶9's "it shall go into its repositories and seek and review"; the faculty enters its repositories to retrieve stored content.
Parallels ¶9's "seek and review and search after"; "search its storehouse" describes the faculty's act of retrieval from its memory-store.
The conditional "if" requires a condition for retrieval; the logical prerequisite throughout the chapter is that the faculty must first have received the impression before it can send it out.
"Takes it in to its inner repository" follows the chapter's consistent pattern of faculties receiving and storing impressions.
"Until" introduces the temporal condition of inquiry, paralleling the pattern in every other faculty description in this chapter.
"Immediately" directly parallels ¶9's "immediately it shall go into its repositories," the formulaic response to inquiry used throughout the chapter.
The cellarman metaphor concludes with retrieval from storage; "It shall find it in the place that it put it" completes the cycle of deposit and recovery.
The definite article "the" introduces "sound" as the specific category belonging to the faculty of the ears, following the established pattern.
The definite article "the" introduces the faculty of smell in the same formulaic pattern as the preceding faculty descriptions.
The preposition "of" connects "entrance" to "the watchposts," following standard possessive construction in the camp/guard metaphor.
"They" refers to the guards who eventually receive the newcomer with great trouble, maintaining the consistent subject of the camp metaphor.
Directly echoes ¶21's own earlier phrasing "the bolts are upon the gates"; door bolts are consistently located "upon the gates" in the camp metaphor.
"Are many" parallels the chapter's repeated emphasis on multiplicity ("many sentinels," "a mass of guards," "many holding rooms").
The definite article "the" before "will of Sin" specifies the particular evil intention being annulled by the Holy Spirit's reign.

"In contrast" marks the antithetical transition from the annulment of Sin's will to the establishment of the Holy Spirit's purpose, expressing the Swedenborgian principle of opposition between the proprium and the Divine influx.
